topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestReorgUnsafeHead`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed by Claude on behalf of @ajsutton.

**CI run:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/123078/workflows/4327c7d8-ab80-44a4-9508-0c99d5bc2fe0/jobs/4868463/tests

**Job:** `memory-all-kona-op-reth` (acceptance tests)
**Date:** 2026-04-21
**Branch:** `gh-readonly-queue/develop/pr-20165-4df50ca0801bf0dd7049995d5a7c8cc8396023df` (merge queue)
**Test file:** `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/reorgs/unsafe_head_test.go:113`

**Error:**
```
Error Trace: /home/circleci/project/op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/reorgs/unsafe_head_test.go:113
Error:       Should not be: 0xae78b3b90db8d7d10c044465707fc30e969695515bb3e778accb1554867a7831
Test:        TestReorgUnsafeHead
Messages:    Expected to get different heads on divergence block number, but got the same hash, so no reorg happened on chain A
```

Preceding log lines:

```
unsafe_head_test.go:111: Reorged chain A on divergence block number (prior the reorg) number=9 head=ae78b3..7a7831 parent=5aaa56..e2828e
unsafe_head_test.go:112: Reorged chain A on divergence block number (after the reorg) number=9 head=ae78b3..7a7831 parent=5aaa56..e2828e
```

**Context:**
- The test was unskipped and migrated to `TwoL2SupernodeInterop` in #20136 (commit `4df50ca080`).
- After `StopSequencer()`, the test uses `op-test-sequencer` to sequence a conflicting block at the unsafe head height, then calls `StartSequencer()` on the CL and waits for a new block.
- At the assertion, the block at the divergence height is still the original block — the EL's view of the unsafe head was never replaced by the test-sequencer's conflicting block (or the CL's resumed sequencing reverted the reorg).
- The test intersperses two `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` calls between `ia.New()` / `ia.Next()` at lines 97 and 101 — likely a timing race.

Will investigate and propose a fix.

topPRs.title: test: reproduce #21663 NUT bundle drift via L2DevFeatureFlags version bump
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Do not merge — diagnostic experiment for the CI failures in ethereum-optimism/optimism#21663.

**What this shows:** the karst/lagoon NUT activation failures come from the **semver downgrade guard** in `L2ContractsManagerUtils.upgradeTo` (reverts `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed` when the installed proxy version > the version the bundle installs), combined with a test-fixture gap: **L2DevFeatureFlags is not captured in any pre-fork state file**, so the NUT activation test rebuilds it from HEAD instead of the fork era.

- Before: HEAD L2DevFeatureFlags = 1.0.0, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.0,1.0.0)=false` → pass.
- After the bump: HEAD = 1.0.1, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.1,1.0.0)=true` → downgrade → revert.

Commits:
1. bump L2DevFeatureFlags semver 1.0.0 → 1.0.1
2. comment-only touch to the NUT test file (contracts-only changes don't set `rust_changes_detected`, so the NUT test would be skipped — a CI gap in its own right)
3. regenerate `current-upgrade-bundle.json`
4. regenerate `semver-lock.json`
5. bump the version unit test to 1.0.1 + re-snapshot the **lagoon** bundle (karst left immutable)

Expected CI after commit 5: snapshot checks + version test green; **lagoon** NUT/interop green (bundle now installs 1.0.1, matching HEAD); **karst** NUT still red (its immutable bundle installs 1.0.0 while the test's HEAD genesis has 1.0.1). Note: `nut-provenance-verify lagoon` will fail because the lock commit is the develop merge-base, which predates the change.

topPRs.title: feat(kona-sp1): scaffold super interop programs
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the initial SP1 super interop proof shape for ZK dispute games.

It introduces shared public IO types for the unified super-range program and final super-aggregation program, including super-root encoding and final public-value encoding that match the tuple verified by `ZKDisputeGame.prove`.

The output-root range and consolidation proofs are now handled by a single unified super-range program with (optimistic output-root) range and consolidation modes, so aggregation verifies one semantic class of proof with one `range_vkey`.

The guest execution logic is intentionally still incomplete in this PR. The aggregation program accepts the range vkey dynamically for now, and the range/consolidation verification bodies are left as TODOs for the follow-up implementation work.

## Program Input Validation

This PR also introduces logic to validate the program input shape. This validation is complementary to the more involved super-STF operations, ensuring that the super-aggregation program verifies that all required proofs are well-formed and provided.

### Super-range input validation

The unified super-range program first validates the mode-specific input shape.
For range mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- chain IDs are non-empty and strictly increasing
- claimed transitions cover exactly every (timestamp, chain_id) pair in span order
- each transition’s timestamp and chain ID match the expected position

For consolidation mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- there is one consolidation input per timestamp
- each claimed super-root proof has the expected timestamp
- each super-root proof uses the supported version and ordered chain set
- optimistic blocks are non-empty, strictly ordered, and match the claimed super-root proof’s chain coverage
- every timestamp uses the same chain set

### Super-aggregation input validation

Aggregation validates the declared range public outputs before recursive proof verification.
It checks:

- `starting_super_root_proof` hashes to `starting_root_hash`
- there is at least one range output and one consolidation output
- the disputed interval starts at `starting_super_root.timestamp + 1`
- consolidation outputs cover the full timestamp interval contiguously
- consolidation `previous_super_root` values chain forward from `starting_root_hash`
- the final consolidated root equals `root_claim`
- range outputs cover the same full timestamp interval contiguously
- every range output commits to the same `l1_head` as the game
- every range output’s `previous_super_root` matches the super root before that range
- range optimistic blocks match the corresponding consolidation optimistic blocks timestamp by timestamp
- all range/consolidation outputs use the chain set from the starting super root

## Meta

part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21459
